result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_df_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get selected nodes as a Polars DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7800-L7905){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_df_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Similar to get_node_df but only exports currently selected nodes. Useful for analyzing subsets of nodes after filtering with selection methods. The DataFrame always includes 'id', 'label', and 'type' as the first three columns, sorted by 'id' in ascending order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : DataFrame with mandatory columns 'id', 'label', 'type' (first three), followed by other attributes and 'degree'. Empty DataFrame if no nodes are selected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - returns empty DataFrame if no nodes are selected - the 'id', 'label', and 'type' columns are always present (first three) - if a node has no label, the label column will contain None - if a node has no type attribute, the type column will contain None - rows are sorted by id in ascending order - use selection methods before calling this - same structure as `get_node_df()` but filtered to selection ## Examples {.doc-examples} Export filtered nodes: ::: {#0766d9b7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(10) .add_path_graph(5) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3) ) df = graph.get_node_df_ws() # Only high-degree nodes in DataFrame; returns number of selected nodes df.shape[0] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Combine selection with DataFrame analysis: ::: {#735e33da .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") graph.select_nodes_by_id([a_id, b_id, c_id]) selected_df = graph.get_node_df_ws() # Analyze just the selected nodes avg_degree = selected_df["degree"].mean() ``` :::
